â€†SMTâ€ƒSoftware Module Testâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€†A full and detailed test of an individual software module in
 â€†â–›â–œâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ isolation; such testing requires that all branches of the

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒIt tests all the interfaces to the module, any data recorded or

â€†SCVâ€ƒSoftware Compatibilityâ€ƒ   â€†A mechanism for verifying that no executable code software 
â•“â•–    Verificationâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€†changes have been made to a module following changes to

â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•

If remote/local mode is enabled (CONFIG_RL_EN = 1), and:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ1.â€ƒ Neither mode_RemoteOn or mode_LocalOn is active, default to remote mode
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ2.â€ƒ A rising edge is detected on mode_LocalOn, reset mode_RemoteOn (in local)
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ3.â€ƒ A rising edge is detected on mode_RemoteOn, reset mode_LocalOn (in remote)
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ4.â€ƒ Both mode_RemoteOn and mode_LocalOn is active, default to remote mode
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="45" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="46" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
If there is no energised position feedback (CONFIG_FBK_ENG_EN = 0), then the energised state 
of the valve is derived from the elapsed time of the operation timer using the following 
formulae:

â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”
â”‚$derived_fbk_eng = 1 when:â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€„â€„â”‚
â”‚â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ wrkTimeFbkEngSim â€†  â”‚
â”‚actual_Operating_Timer â‰¤ TIME_ENG_MAX â”€ TIME_ENG_MAX â•³ ----------------------------------------â€„â”‚
â”‚â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ 100â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ    â”‚
â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜
Note:  â€ƒâ€ƒwrkTimeFbkEngSim is the error checked equivalent of TIME_DER_ENG

If the calculated elapsed time is close to or less than k_TIME_OP_MIN (210ms),
the calculated elapsed time (calEngElapsedTime) is set to k_TIME_OP_MIN. This ensures at
least one timing pulse is required before the timer reaches zero.

The derived energised signal ($derived_fbk_eng) is reset if the valve is requested to be 
deenergised ($ctrl_EngDeng = 0).
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>

          </MultilingualText>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="4A" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="4B" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
If there is no deenergised position feedback (CONFIG_FBK_DENG_EN = 0), then the deenergised 
state of the valve is derived from the elapsed time of the operation timer using the following 
formulae:

â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”
â”‚$derived_fbk_deng = 1 when:â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€†  â€†â”‚
â”‚â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  wrkTimeFbkDengSim  â€„â€†â”‚
â”‚actual_Operating_Timer â‰¤ TIME_DENG_MAX â”€ TIME_DENG_MAX â•³ ------------------------------------------- â”‚
â”‚â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ 100â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ        â”‚
â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜
Note:  â€ƒâ€ƒwrkTimeFbkDengSim is the error checked equivalent of TIME_DER_DENG

If the calculated elapsed time is close to or less than k_TIME_OP_MIN (210ms),
the calculated elapsed time (calDengElapsedTime) is set to k_TIME_OP_MIN. This ensures at
least one timing pulse is required before the timer reaches zero.

The derived deenergised signal ($derived_fbk_deng) is reset if the valve is requested to be 
energised ($ctrl_EngDeng = 1).
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

                  <Text>Signal Conditioning â€” Derived deenergised position</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>

If simulation mode is active, the simulated energised position signal is set as follows:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒmode_SimValue = 0 (no feedback), $sim_fbk_eng = 0

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒmode_SimValue = 1 (permanently energised), $sim_fbk_eng = 1

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒmode_SimValue = 2 (permanently deenergised), $sim_fbk_eng = 0

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒmode_SimValue = 3 (follow demand), $sim_fbk_eng = $ctrl_EngDeng

If simulation mode is not active,  $sim_fbk_eng = 0
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>

                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
If simulation mode is active, the simulated deenergised position signal is set as follows:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒmode_SimValue = 0 (no feedback), $sim_fbk_deng = 0

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒmode_SimValue = 1 (permanently energised), $sim_fbk_deng = 0

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒmode_SimValue = 2 (permanently deenergised), $sim_fbk_deng = 1

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒmode_SimValue = 3 (follow demand), $sim_fbk_deng = NOT $ctrl_EngDeng

If simulation mode is not active,  $sim_fbk_deng = 0
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

                  <Text>Signal Conditioning â€” Simulation mode â€” Deenergised signal</Text>
                </AttributeList>

            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="59" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="5A" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
Generates a working energised signal (wrkEng), that is then used throughout the module as the 
definitive energised position feedback signal.

The energised signal will be either :

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ1.â€ƒâ€†The same as the FBK_ENG parameter if this is in use 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ(CONFIG_FBK_ENG_EN = 1)

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ2.â€ƒâ€†The internally derived energised state (based on the requested state of the valve) 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒif the FBK_ENG signal is NOT in use (CONFIG_FBK_ENG_EN = 0)

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ3.â€ƒâ€†The simulated state of the valve if simulation mode is active (mode_SimOn = 1)

If an actual energised position signal is provided to the module via the FBK_ENG parameter 
(i.e. if CONFIG_FBK_ENG_EN = 1) then wrkEng is set to match the FBK_ENG signal 
(wrkEng = FBK_ENG).

If a derived energised signal is to be used (i.e. if CONFIG_FBK_ENG_EN = 0), then wrkEng is set to 
match the internally derived $derived_fbk_eng signal (wrkEng = $derived_fbk_eng). 
$derived_fbk_eng is based on the requested state of the valve. 

Finally, if simulation mode is active (mode_SimOn = 1), then wrkEng is set to match the internal 
simulation signal $sim_fbk_eng signal (wrkEng = $sim_fbk_eng).
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
          <MultilingualText ID="5B" CompositionName="Title">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="5C" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>Signal conditioning â€” Determine valve ENG position status</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
        </ObjectList>
      </SW.Blocks.CompileUnit>

            <ObjectList>

                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
Generates a working deenergised signal (wrkDeng), that is then used throughout the module 
as the definitive deenergised position feedback signal.

The deenergised signal will be either :

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ1.â€ƒâ€†The same as the FBK_DENG parameter if this is in use 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ(CONFIG_FBK_DENG_EN = 1)

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ2.â€ƒâ€†The internally derived deenergised state (based on the requested state of the valve) 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒif the FBK_DENG signal is NOT in use (CONFIG_FBK_DENG_EN = 0)

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ3.â€ƒâ€†The simulated state of the valve if simulation mode is active (mode_SimOn = 1)

If an actual deenergised position signal is provided to the module via the FBK_DENG parameter 
(i.e. if CONFIG_FBK_DENG_EN = 1) then wrkDeng is set to match the FBK_DENG signal 
wrkDeng = FBK_DENG).

If a derived deenergised signal is to be used (i.e. if CONFIG_FBK_DENG_EN = 0), then wrkDeng is 
set to match the internally derived $derived_fbk_deng signal 
(wrkDeng = $derived_fbk_deng). $derived_fbk_deng is based on the requested state of 
the valve.

Finally, if simulation mode is active (mode_SimOn = 1), then wrkDeng is set to match the 
internal simulation signal $sim_fbk_deng signal (wrkDeng = $sim_fbk_deng). 
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>
                </AttributeList>

            </ObjectList>

            <ObjectList>

                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
Establishes the priority of signal that has control of the valve, the priorities are assigned as 
follows:

â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒSIGNAL TYPEâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒPRIORITYâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒASSIGNED VALUEâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€†CAN BE BYPASSED
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒEmergency Stopâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   Highâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ 40â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€†   NO
â€ƒTripâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ†‘â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€†30â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€†â€†YES
â€ƒInterlockâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€†â†‘â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€†20â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€†â€†YES
â€ƒPermissiveâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€„â€„â†‘â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€†  10â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€†â€†YES
â€ƒAuto/manual controlâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒLowâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€†00â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€†   NO
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒHigh priority signal take precedence over lower priority signals.

Determine a priority 40 (valve safety (or fault) condition is active)

The priority is active if:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ1.â€ƒâ€†The valve is in a fault condition (status_Fault = 1)

â€ƒâ€ƒOR both the following are true

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ1.â€ƒâ€†Safety signals are not disabled (CONFIG_ESTOP_DIS = 0)

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ2.â€ƒâ€†The E_STOP signal is active
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

                  <Text>Signal conditioning â€” Establish control priority (priority 40 safety or fault - highest)</Text>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="90" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="91" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
If  a priority 10 (permissive) condition is active, set the valve to the required state:


PERMITTED STATE IS ENERGISED â€” CONDITIONS:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒIf the Permitted state is energised and Aut/Man request is for energised
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒset the valve to be energised[Branch 1]

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒIf the Permitted state is energised and Aut/Man request is for deenergised and the 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒcurrent valve output matches this state (deenergised) set the valve to be 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒdeenergised (maintain the current state) [Branch 6]

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒIf the Permitted state is energised and Aut/Man request is for deenergised and the 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒcurrent valve output matches the deenergised state, set the valve to be energised 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ(override the auto/man request [Branch 2]

PERMITTED STATE IS DEENERGISED â€” CONDITIONS:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒIf the Permitted state is deenergised and Aut/Man request is for deenergised,
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒset the valve to be  deenergised [Branch 4]

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒIf the Permitted state is deenergised and Aut/Man request is for energised, and the 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒcurrent valve output matches this state (energised) set the valve to be energised 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ(maintain the current state) [Branch 3]

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒIf the Permitted state is deenergised and Aut/Man request is for energised, and the current
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒvalve output matches the deenergised  state, set the valve to be deenergised 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ(override the auto/man request [Branch 5]
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>Control â€” Evaluate priority signals and set eng/deng request (Priority 10)</Text>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="9A" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="9B" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
If a change of state is detected on ctrl_EngDeng, in this case a rising edge indicating the
valve has been requested to change from a deenergised to an energised state, the status of the
valve is set to energising and the energising operation time is loaded into the operation timer.

If the energising operation time is less than k_TIME_OP_MIN (210ms), the 
actual_Operating_Timer is set to k_TIME_OP_MIN. This ensure that at least one timing pulse is 
required, before the timer reaches a value of zero (i.e. at least one controller cycle will be 
required).

If the valve is in a fault condition (status_Fault = true), the change of state is not evaluated
until the fault condition has cleared

Note: the timer is also triggered if the Reset signal is received and the valve is requested to be 
           energised

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="9F" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="A0" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
If a change of state is detected on ctrl_EngDeng, in this case a falling edge indicating the
valve has been requested to change from an energised to a deenergised state, the status of the
valve is set to deenergising and the deenergising operation time is loaded into the operation 
timer.

If the deenergising operation time is less than k_TIME_OP_MIN (210ms), the 
actual_Operating_Timer is set to k_TIME_OP_MIN. This ensure that at least one timing pulse is 
required, before the timer reaches a value of zero (i.e. at least one controller cycle will be 
required).

If the valve is in a fault condition (status_Fault = true), the change of state is not evaluated
until the fault condition has cleared

Note: the timer is also triggered if the Reset signal is received and the valve is requested to be 
           deenergised
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
          <MultilingualText ID="A1" CompositionName="Title">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="A2" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>Check for change of state request â€” Deenergising</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
        </ObjectList>

                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€

is in a static state (i.e. not energising or deenergising), this ensures a clean transition if the 
CONFIG_FBK_ENG_EN signal changes state during runtime.

                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
The valve is confirmed energised (status_Energised = 1) if there is positive indication of the 
energised state (wrkEng = 1) and not of the deenergised signal (wrkDeng = 0). 

I.e. the valve is showing energised and not deenergised
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>

                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
The valve is confirmed deenergised (status_Deenergised = 1) if there is positive indication of the 
deenergised state (wrkDeng = 1) and not of the energised signal (wrkEng = 0). 

I.e. the valve is showing deenergised and not energised
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="B8" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="B9" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
If the valve is in a static state, operation timer = 0 and the valve is not already in a fault
condition, the failed while energised and failed  while deenergised alarms are generated as 
follows:

If the valve is energised (ctrl_EngDeng = 1) and the valve is not energised 
(status_Energised = 0), the failed while energised alarm is generated

If the valve is deenergised (ctrl_EngDeng = 0) and the valve is not deenergised 
(status_Deenergised = 0), the failed while deenergised alarm is generated
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="BD" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="BE" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
If the valve is energising or deenergising decrement the current operation timer value on each 
200ms pulse.

If the timer reaches zero, and the valve is energising, generate the failed to energise alarm.

If the timer reaches zero, and the valve is deenergising, generate the failed to deenergise alarm
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>
                </AttributeList>

            </ObjectList>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="C2" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="C3" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
Stores that last good operation timer elapsed time, this is the elapsed value of the 
actual_Operating_Timer when the valve achieved the correct position. The result is subtracted
from the TIME_ENG/DENG_MAX value to give the true time to achieve position. The result
is stored in actual_Last_Op_Time

If the valve were energising, then actual_Last_Op_Time is calculated as follows:

â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”
â”‚actual_Last_Op_Time = TIME_ENG_MAX â”€ actual_Operating_Timerâ€„ â€†â€†â”‚
â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜

If the valve were deenergising, then actual_Last_Op_Time is calculated as follows:

â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”
â”‚actual_Last_Op_Time = TIME_DENG_MAX â”€ actual_Operating_Timerâ€„   â€†â”‚
â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜

If the valve either fails to energise or fails to deenergise, then actual_Last_Op_Time is set 
to -1.0 to indicate a fault state.
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
          <MultilingualText ID="C4" CompositionName="Title">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="C5" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>Calculate last operation timer value</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
        </ObjectList>
      </SW.Blocks.CompileUnit>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="CC" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="CD" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
If the RESET signal is active, reset all position derived alarms and also clear the RESET signal.

If the actual_Last_Op time is at -1.0 (indicating the valve is in a fault condition), the 
actual_Last_Op will be set to zero if a reset pulse is received. This ensures that a valve that was 
in fault, but is now in the correct deenergised state when reset, generates an 
actual_Last_Op value of zero.
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
The status signals for faults, alarms and warnings are either duplicates of the message signals 
(signals beginning with msg_) or logical combinations of them.

The following is a full list of the status signals:

â€ƒUT31001_Dy_DevValveIsolâ€ƒ(full contents)
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒSIGNAL NAMEâ€†   â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒFUNCTION  â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒTYPE
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒstatus_Operatingâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€„STATUS â€” Valve is changing stateâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€†Bool
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   (1 = changing state, 0 = fixed state)
â€ƒstatus_Faultâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ     â€†STATUS â€” Valve is in fault â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€†Bool
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   (1 = fault present, 0 = healthy)
â€ƒstatus_OperateOnâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€„STATUS â€” Valve output is on â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€„Bool
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   (1 = energised, 0 = deenergised)
â€ƒstatus_Autâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€„STATUS â€” Automatic mode active â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  Bool
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   (1 = auto mode on, 0 = auto mode off)
â€ƒstatus_Manâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€†STATUS â€” Manual mode active â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€„Bool
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   (1 = man mode on, 0 = man mode off)
â€ƒstatus_EStopâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€†STATUS â€” E_STOP safety signal is active  â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€„Bool
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   (1 = active, 0 = healthy)
â€ƒstatus_Tripâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒSTATUS â€” TRIP signal is active  â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€†Bool
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   (1 = active, 0 = healthy)
â€ƒstatus_Ilockâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€†â€„STATUS â€” INTERLOCK signal is active  â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ    Bool
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   (1 = active, 0 = healthy)
â€ƒstatus_Permâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ STATUS â€” PERMISSIVE signal is active  â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€†Bool
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   (1 = active, 0 = healthy)
â€ƒstatus_BypassOnâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€„STATUS â€” Valve is in bypass modeâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€†Bool

â€ƒstatus_SimOnâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ     â€„STATUS â€” Valve is in simulation mode          â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€†Bool
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   (1 = Simulation mode, 0 = normal)
â€ƒstatus_RemoteOnâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€„STATUS â€” Valve is in remote mode          â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€†Bool
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   (1 = Remote mode, 0 = normal)

TITLE = 'Ð ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»ÑÑ‚Ð¾Ñ€ Ñ‚Ñ€ÐµÑ…Ð¿Ð¾Ð·Ð¸Ñ†Ð¸Ð¾Ð½Ð½Ñ‹Ð¹.'

{ S7_read_back := 'true' ;
  S7_blockview := 'big'  }

AUTHOR  : VA
FAMILY  : LIB_PLC
VERSION : '2.2'

VAR_INPUT // Ð’Ñ…Ð¾Ð´Ð½Ñ‹Ðµ Ð¿ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ¼ÐµÐ½Ð½Ñ‹Ðµ, ÑÐ¾Ñ…Ñ€Ð°Ð½ÑÐµÐ¼Ñ‹Ðµ.
PV      :REAL := 0.0; // Ð˜Ð·Ð¼ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ½Ð½Ð¾Ðµ Ð·Ð½Ð°Ñ‡ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ Ñ€ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»Ð¸Ñ€ÑƒÐµÐ¼Ð¾Ð³Ð¾ Ð¿Ð°Ñ€Ð°Ð¼ÐµÑ‚Ñ€Ð°.
SP      :REAL := 0.0; // Ð—Ð°Ð´Ð°Ð½Ð½Ð¾Ðµ Ð·Ð½Ð°Ñ‡ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ Ñ€ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»Ð¸Ñ€ÑƒÐµÐ¼Ð¾Ð³Ð¾ Ð¿Ð°Ñ€Ð°Ð¼ÐµÑ‚Ñ€Ð°.
DBand   :REAL := 2.0; // Ð—Ð¾Ð½Ð° Ð½ÐµÑ‡ÑƒÐ²ÑÑ‚Ð²Ð¸Ñ‚ÐµÐ»ÑŒÐ½Ð¾ÑÑ‚Ð¸ > 0.
HystPos :REAL := 1.0; // Ð“Ð¸ÑÑ‚ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ·Ð¸Ñ > 0.
HystNeg :REAL := 1.0; // Ð“Ð¸ÑÑ‚ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ·Ð¸Ñ > 0.
END_VAR

VAR_OUTPUT // Ð’Ñ‹Ñ…Ð¾Ð´Ð½Ñ‹Ðµ Ð¿ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ¼ÐµÐ½Ð½Ñ‹Ðµ, ÑÐ¾Ñ…Ñ€Ð°Ð½ÑÐµÐ¼Ñ‹Ðµ.
OpPos :BOOL :=FALSE; // Ð’Ñ‹Ñ…Ð¾Ð´ ÑƒÐ¿Ñ€Ð°Ð²Ð»ÑÑŽÑ‰ÐµÐ³Ð¾ ÑÐ¸Ð³Ð½Ð°Ð»Ð° Ð¿Ð¾Ð»Ð¾Ð¶Ð¸Ñ‚ÐµÐ»ÑŒÐ½Ñ‹Ð¹.
OpNeg :BOOL :=FALSE; // Ð’Ñ‹Ñ…Ð¾Ð´ ÑƒÐ¿Ñ€Ð°Ð²Ð»ÑÑŽÑ‰ÐµÐ³Ð¾ ÑÐ¸Ð³Ð½Ð°Ð»Ð° Ð¾Ñ‚Ñ€Ð¸Ñ†Ð°Ñ‚ÐµÐ»ÑŒÐ½Ñ‹Ð¹.
END_VAR

VAR // Ð’Ð½ÑƒÑ‚Ñ€ÐµÐ½Ð½Ð¸Ðµ Ð¿ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ¼ÐµÐ½Ð½Ñ‹Ðµ, ÑÐ¾Ñ…Ñ€Ð°Ð½ÑÐµÐ¼Ñ‹Ðµ.
ER :REAL := 0.0; // ÐžÑˆÐ¸Ð±ÐºÐ° Ñ€ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»Ð¸Ñ€Ð¾Ð²Ð°Ð½Ð¸Ñ.
END_VAR

BEGIN

// Ð ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»ÑÑ‚Ð¾Ñ€ Ñ‚Ñ€ÐµÑ…Ð¿Ð¾Ð·Ð¸Ñ†Ð¸Ð¾Ð½Ð½Ñ‹Ð¹.
//       Db3PosControl
//     +---------------+
//     | Fb3PosControl |
//  ->-|PV        OpPos|->-
//    -|SP        OpNeg|->-
//    -|DBand          |
//    -|HystPos        |
//    -|HystNeg        |
//     +---------------+

// ÐžÑˆÐ¸Ð±ÐºÐ° Ñ€ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»Ð¸Ñ€Ð¾Ð²Ð°Ð½Ð¸Ñ.
ER := SP - PV;

// Ð’ÐšÐ› Ð½Ð°Ð³Ñ€ÐµÐ² Ð¸Ð»Ð¸ Ð´Ð²Ð¸Ð¶ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ Ð²Ð¿ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ´.
IF (ER >= (DBand + HystPos))
THEN
OpPos := TRUE;
END_IF;

// Ð’Ð«ÐšÐ› Ð½Ð°Ð³Ñ€ÐµÐ² Ð¸Ð»Ð¸ Ð´Ð²Ð¸Ð¶ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ Ð²Ð¿ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ´.
IF (ER <= (DBand - HystPos))
THEN
OpPos := FALSE;
END_IF;

// Ð’ÐšÐ› Ð¾Ñ…Ð»Ð°Ð¶Ð´ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ Ð¸Ð»Ð¸ Ð´Ð²Ð¸Ð¶ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ Ð½Ð°Ð·Ð°Ð´.
IF (ER <= (0.0 - DBand - HystNeg))
THEN
OpNeg := TRUE;
END_IF;

// Ð’Ð«ÐšÐ› Ð¾Ñ…Ð»Ð°Ð¶Ð´ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ Ð¸Ð»Ð¸ Ð´Ð²Ð¸Ð¶ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ Ð½Ð°Ð·Ð°Ð´.
IF (ER >= (0.0 - DBand + HystNeg))
THEN
OpNeg := FALSE;
END_IF;

// ÐŸÑ€Ð¸Ð¼ÐµÐ½ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ.
//
// Ð¢Ñ€ÐµÑ…Ð¿Ð¾Ð·Ð¸Ñ†Ð¸Ð¾Ð½Ð½Ñ‹Ð¹ Ñ€ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»ÑÑ‚Ð¾Ñ€ Ð¸ÑÐ¿Ð¾Ð»ÑŒÐ·ÑƒÐµÑ‚ÑÑ ÐºÐ°Ðº Ð¿Ñ€Ð¾ÑÑ‚ÐµÐ¹ÑˆÐ¸Ð¹ Ñ€ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»ÑÑ‚Ð¾Ñ€ Ñ‚ÐµÐ¼Ð¿ÐµÑ€Ð°Ñ‚ÑƒÑ€Ñ‹ Ð¸Ð»Ð¸ Ð¿Ð¾Ð»Ð¾Ð¶ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ñ.

// Ð¡Ñ‚Ð°Ñ‚Ð¸Ñ‡ÐµÑÐºÐ°Ñ Ñ…Ð°Ñ€Ð°ÐºÑ‚ÐµÑ€Ð¸ÑÑ‚Ð¸ÐºÐ°.
//
//                           OpPos
//                             ^
//                             |  DBand
//                             |<-------->|
//                             |          |
//                             |   HystPos|HystPos
//                             |   |<---->|<---->|
//                             |   |      |      |
//                            1|---***<***1***<******
//                             |   *      |      *
//                             |   v      |      ^
//                             |   *      |      *
// -ER <-----***<*******<******0******>*******>***-----> +ER
//           *      |      *   |
//           v      |      ^   |
//           *      |      *   |
//        ******>***1***>***---|-1
//           |      |      |   |
//           |<---->|<---->|   |
//           HystHeg|HystHeg   |
//                  |          |
//                  |<-------->|
//                     DBand   |
//                             v
//                           OpNeg

// Ð¡Ñ…ÐµÐ¼Ð° Ð²ÐºÐ»ÑŽÑ‡ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ñ.
//
//        +---------------+     +-------------+     +-------------+
// SP-->--|SP        OpPos|-->--| ÐÐ°Ð³Ñ€ÐµÐ²Ð°Ñ‚ÐµÐ»ÑŒ |-->--| Ð”Ð°Ñ‚Ñ‡Ð¸Ðº      |--+-->PV
//        |               |     +-------------+     | Ñ‚ÐµÐ¼Ð¿ÐµÑ€Ð°Ñ‚ÑƒÑ€Ñ‹ |  |
//        |               |                         |             |  |
//        |               |     +-------------+     |             |  |
//     +--|PV        OpNeg|-->--| ÐžÑ…Ð»Ð°Ð´Ð¸Ñ‚ÐµÐ»ÑŒ  |-->--|             |  |
//     |  +---------------+     +-------------+     +-------------+  |
//     |                                                             |
//     +-------------------------------------------------------------+
//
//        +---------------+     +--------------+     +-------------+
// SP-->--|SP        OpPos|-->--| ÐœÐ¾Ñ‚Ð¾Ñ€ Ð²Ð¿ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ´ |-->--| Ð”Ð°Ñ‚Ñ‡Ð¸Ðº      |--+-->PV
//        |               |     +--------------+     | Ð¿Ð¾Ð»Ð¾Ð¶ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ñ   |  |
//        |               |                          |             |  |
//        |               |     +--------------+     |             |  |
//     +--|PV        OpNeg|-->--| ÐœÐ¾Ñ‚Ð¾Ñ€ Ð½Ð°Ð·Ð°Ð´  |-->--|             |  |
//     |  +---------------+     +--------------+     +-------------+  |
//     |                                                              |
//     +--------------------------------------------------------------+

plc-study-library/ç‰‡æ®µ/02_è®¾å¤‡æŽ§åˆ¶/ä½ç½®æŽ§åˆ¶_ä¸¤ç‚¹å¼.sclFUNCTION_BLOCK "Fb2PosControl"
TITLE = 'Ð ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»ÑÑ‚Ð¾Ñ€ Ð´Ð²ÑƒÑ…Ð¿Ð¾Ð·Ð¸Ñ†Ð¸Ð¾Ð½Ð½Ñ‹Ð¹.'

{ S7_read_back := 'true' ;
  S7_blockview := 'big'  }

AUTHOR  : VA
FAMILY  : LIB_PLC
VERSION : '2.1'

VAR_INPUT // Ð’Ñ…Ð¾Ð´Ð½Ñ‹Ðµ Ð¿ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ¼ÐµÐ½Ð½Ñ‹Ðµ, ÑÐ¾Ñ…Ñ€Ð°Ð½ÑÐµÐ¼Ñ‹Ðµ.
PV   :REAL := 0.0; // Ð˜Ð·Ð¼ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ½Ð½Ð¾Ðµ Ð·Ð½Ð°Ñ‡ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ Ñ€ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»Ð¸Ñ€ÑƒÐµÐ¼Ð¾Ð³Ð¾ Ð¿Ð°Ñ€Ð°Ð¼ÐµÑ‚Ñ€Ð°.
SP   :REAL := 0.0; // Ð—Ð°Ð´Ð°Ð½Ð½Ð¾Ðµ Ð·Ð½Ð°Ñ‡ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ Ñ€ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»Ð¸Ñ€ÑƒÐµÐ¼Ð¾Ð³Ð¾ Ð¿Ð°Ñ€Ð°Ð¼ÐµÑ‚Ñ€Ð°.
HYST :REAL := 5.0; // Ð“Ð¸ÑÑ‚ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ·Ð¸Ñ > 0.
END_VAR

VAR_OUTPUT // Ð’Ñ‹Ñ…Ð¾Ð´Ð½Ñ‹Ðµ Ð¿ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ¼ÐµÐ½Ð½Ñ‹Ðµ, ÑÐ¾Ñ…Ñ€Ð°Ð½ÑÐµÐ¼Ñ‹Ðµ.
OP :BOOL := FALSE; // Ð’Ñ‹Ñ…Ð¾Ð´ ÑƒÐ¿Ñ€Ð°Ð²Ð»ÑÑŽÑ‰ÐµÐ³Ð¾ ÑÐ¸Ð³Ð½Ð°Ð»Ð°.
END_VAR

VAR // Ð’Ð½ÑƒÑ‚Ñ€ÐµÐ½Ð½Ð¸Ðµ Ð¿ÐµÑ€ÐµÐ¼ÐµÐ½Ð½Ñ‹Ðµ, ÑÐ¾Ñ…Ñ€Ð°Ð½ÑÐµÐ¼Ñ‹Ðµ.
ER :REAL := 0.0; // ÐžÑˆÐ¸Ð±ÐºÐ° Ñ€ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»Ð¸Ñ€Ð¾Ð²Ð°Ð½Ð¸Ñ.
END_VAR

BEGIN

// Ð ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»ÑÑ‚Ð¾Ñ€ Ð´Ð²ÑƒÑ…Ð¿Ð¾Ð·Ð¸Ñ†Ð¸Ð¾Ð½Ð½Ñ‹Ð¹.
//       Db2PosControl
//     +---------------+
//     | Fb2PosControl |
//  ->-|PV           OP|->-
//    -|SP             |
//    -|HYST           |
//     +---------------+

// ÐžÑˆÐ¸Ð±ÐºÐ° Ñ€ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»Ð¸Ñ€Ð¾Ð²Ð°Ð½Ð¸Ñ.
ER := SP - PV;

// Ð ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»ÑÑ‚Ð¾Ñ€ Ð´Ð²ÑƒÑ…Ð¿Ð¾Ð·Ð¸Ñ†Ð¸Ð¾Ð½Ð½Ñ‹Ð¹.
IF (ER >= HYST) THEN
OP:=TRUE;
END_IF;

IF (ER <= HYST * (-1.0)) THEN
OP := FALSE;
END_IF;

// ÐŸÑ€Ð¸Ð¼ÐµÐ½ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ.
//
// Ð”Ð²ÑƒÑ…Ð¿Ð¾Ð·Ð¸Ñ†Ð¸Ð¾Ð½Ð½Ñ‹Ð¹ Ñ€ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»ÑÑ‚Ð¾Ñ€ Ð¸ÑÐ¿Ð¾Ð»ÑŒÐ·ÑƒÐµÑ‚ÑÑ ÐºÐ°Ðº Ð¿Ñ€Ð¾ÑÑ‚ÐµÐ¹ÑˆÐ¸Ð¹ Ñ€ÐµÐ³ÑƒÐ»ÑÑ‚Ð¾Ñ€ Ñ‚ÐµÐ¼Ð¿ÐµÑ€Ð°Ñ‚ÑƒÑ€Ñ‹, Ð´Ð°Ð²Ð»ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ñ, ÑƒÑ€Ð¾Ð²Ð½Ñ.

// Ð£ÑÐ»Ð¾Ð²Ð½Ð¾Ðµ Ð³Ñ€Ð°Ñ„Ð¸Ñ‡ÐµÑÐºÐ¾Ðµ Ð¾Ð±Ð¾Ð·Ð½Ð°Ñ‡ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ðµ.
//
//      +---------------+
//      |               |
//      |    +--<--+--  |
//      |    |     |    |
// ER->-|    v     ^    |->-OP
//      |    |     |    |
//      |  --+-->--+    |
//      |               |
//      +---------------+

// Ð¡Ñ‚Ð°Ñ‚Ð¸Ñ‡ÐµÑÐºÐ°Ñ Ñ…Ð°Ñ€Ð°ÐºÑ‚ÐµÑ€Ð¸ÑÑ‚Ð¸ÐºÐ°.
//
//                 OP
//                  ^
//                  |
//           ***<***1***<******
//           *      |      *
//           v      |      ^
//           *      |      *
// -ER <--******>***0***>***--> +ER
//           |      |      |
//           |<---->|<---->|
//             HYST   HYST

// Ð’Ñ€ÐµÐ¼ÐµÐ½Ð½Ð°Ñ Ñ…Ð°Ñ€Ð°ÐºÑ‚ÐµÑ€Ð¸ÑÑ‚Ð¸ÐºÐ°.
//
// ^ PV,SP
// |         PV
// |----------*---------------*------
// |         * *             * *   |
// |        *   *           *   *  |  SP + HYST
// |       *     *         *       |
// |======*=======*=======*========== SP
// |     *         *     *         |
// |    *           *   *          |  SP - HYST
// |   *             * *           |
// |--*---------------*--------------
// | * 
// |*
// +-----------------------------------------> t[s]
//
// ^ OP
// |
// 1***********       *********
// |          *       *       *
// 0----------*********-------***------------> t[s]

// Ð¡Ñ…ÐµÐ¼Ð° Ð²ÐºÐ»ÑŽÑ‡ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ñ.
//
//                  +---------------+
//                  |               |   ÐžÐ±ÑŠÐµÐºÑ‚ ÑƒÐ¿Ñ€Ð°Ð²Ð»ÐµÐ½Ð¸Ñ
//                  |    +--<--+--  |     +-----------+
//        +---+ ER  |    |     |    | OP  |     K     |
// SP-->--| + |-->--|    v     ^    |-->--| --------- |-->--+-->PV
// PV  +--| - |     |    |     |    |     | T * s + 1 |     |
//     |  +---+     |  --+-->--+    |     +-----------+     |
//     |            |               |                       |
//     |            +---------------+                       |
//     |                                                    |
//     +----------------------------------------------------+

plc-study-library/ç‰‡æ®µ/02_è®¾å¤‡æŽ§åˆ¶/å†·å´å¡”å¾ªçŽ¯.sclï»¿FUNCTION_BLOCK "CoolingTowerCirculation"
{ S7_Optimized_Access := 'TRUE' }
AUTHOR : 'Searinox(Gerrit_Vogtlaender)'
FAMILY : AKK
VERSION : 0.1
   VAR_INPUT 
      iBranch : Bool;   // Strang
      iPumpCoolWater1 : "Pump";
      iPumpCoolWater2 : "Pump";
      iFlowTempPlant : Real;   // Vorlauftemperatur
      iSetPointMin : Real;
      iSetPointMax : Real;
      iPumpCoolWater1Run : Bool;
      iPumpCoolWater2Run : Bool;
      iPumpCoolWater1Err : Bool;
      iPumpCoolWater1Err_1 : Bool;
      iBleedingUnitCirculatingPumpRun : Bool;
      iCt1SprayPipeIsOpen : Bool;
      iCt2SprayPipeIsOpen : Bool;
   END_VAR

   VAR_OUTPUT 
      oPumpCoolWater1 : Bool;
      oPumpCoolWater2 : Bool;
      oCt1Fan : Bool;
      oCt2Fan : Bool;
      oCt1FanSetPoint : Int;
      oCt2FanSetPoint : Int;
      oCt1SprayPipeOpen : Bool;
      oCt2SprayPipeOpen : Bool;
   END_VAR

   VAR 
      sPump1 : Bool;
      sPump2 : Bool;
      sTooCold : Bool;
      sTooHot : Bool;
      sSetPoint : Int;
      sVentilatoPt : Time := T#30S;
      sBothPump : Bool;
      sOverRunTime : Time := T#10S;
      RunPumpsRedundantly : "RunPumpsRedundantly";
      IEC_TMR_0 {OriginalPartName := 'IEC_TIMER'; LibVersion := '1.0'} : IEC_TIMER;
      IEC_TMR_1 {OriginalPartName := 'IEC_TIMER'; LibVersion := '1.0'} : IEC_TIMER;
      sVentilator1Et : Time;
      sVentilator2Et : Time;
      sSetPointMin : Int := 0;
      sSetPointMax : Int := 27648;
      sMaxThreshold : Real := 1.0;
      IEC_TMR_2 {OriginalPartName := 'IEC_TIMER'; LibVersion := '1.0'} : IEC_TIMER;
      s_AbsalzPulsePT : Time := T#5m;
      s_AbsalzTP : Bool;
      s_AbsalzPulseET : Time;
   END_VAR


BEGIN
	#sBothPump := #iFlowTempPlant > (#iSetPointMax + #sMaxThreshold) OR #s_AbsalzTP;
	
	#RunPumpsRedundantly(i_strang := #iBranch,
	                     i_beide := #sBothPump,
	                     i_err1 := #iPumpCoolWater1Err,
	                     i_err2 := #iPumpCoolWater1Err_1,
	                     i_run1 := #iPumpCoolWater1Run,
	                     i_run2 := #iPumpCoolWater2Run,
	                     i_tof_pt := #sOverRunTime,
	                     o_p1 => #oPumpCoolWater1,
	                     o_p2 => #oPumpCoolWater2,
	                     io_s_p1 := #sPump1,
	                     io_s_p2 := #sPump2);
	
	#IEC_TMR_0.TON(IN := #iPumpCoolWater1Run AND NOT #sTooCold,
	               PT := #sVentilatoPt,
	               Q => #oCt1Fan,
	               ET => #sVentilator1Et);
	
	#IEC_TMR_1.TON(IN := #iPumpCoolWater2Run AND NOT #sTooCold,
	               PT := #sVentilatoPt,
	               Q => #oCt2Fan,
	               ET => #sVentilator2Et);
	
	#IEC_TMR_2.TP(IN := #iBleedingUnitCirculatingPumpRun,
	              PT := #s_AbsalzPulsePT,
	              Q => #s_AbsalzTP,
	              ET => #s_AbsalzPulseET);
	
	#sTooCold := #iFlowTempPlant <= #iSetPointMin;
	#sTooHot := #iFlowTempPlant >= #iSetPointMax;
	
	IF #sTooHot THEN
	    #sSetPoint := #sSetPointMax;
	ELSIF #sTooCold THEN
	    #sSetPoint := #sSetPointMin;
	ELSE
	    #sSetPoint := "ScaleValueRealToInt"(iVal := #iFlowTempPlant,
	                                        iXMin := #iSetPointMin,
	                                        iXMax := #iSetPointMax,
	                                        iYMin := #sSetPointMin,
	                                        iYMax := #sSetPointMax);
	END_IF;
	
	#oCt1FanSetPoint := #sSetPoint;
	#oCt2FanSetPoint := #sSetPoint;
	#oCt1SprayPipeOpen := #oPumpCoolWater1;
	#oCt2SprayPipeOpen := #oPumpCoolWater2;
	
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FC18001_StdSubScaleAI is a subroutine block that is used to scale the integer signal from an 
analog instrument, in the form of an input word (IW).

The resultant scaled value is a real (floating point) number that matches the calibrated range 
of the instrument.

The block monitors the instrument to see if the scaled value is out-of-range, the following three 
fault signals are generated:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒOver-range (signal is more than a specified percentage above the calibrated 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒrange of the instrument

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒUnder-range (signal is more than a specified percentage below the calibrated 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒrange of the instrument

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒCommon out-of-range, either the over-range or under-range fault is active

This is a subroutine block.

1.â€†â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒFUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION


FC18001 is the Analog Input Scale block, it is a comprehensive block designed to read and scale 
an analog instrument; it provides the following broad functions:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒRead an analog input, convert it to a real number that represents the calibrated 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒrange of the instrument in engineering units

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒGenerate fault signals if the instrument is out of range



â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚
1.1â€„ â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒRead and scale and instrument signal


The principal function of the block is to read a raw integer signal from an analog instrument 
(in the form of an input word, IW), and convert it into a scaled, floating point (real) number that 
reflects the calibrated reading of the instrument in question.

For example, if a flow meter with a calibrated range of -100 l/s to +100 l/s provided a 4-20 mA 
signal to the PLC, then 4 mA would represent -100 l/s and 20 mA would represent +100 l/s.

A typical 4-20 mA analog input signal returns a raw value of 0 at 4 mA and 27648 at 20 mA.â€ƒ

The block would return scaled values as follows (it would also return every value in between; five 
typical values have been shown):

1.2â€„ â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒFault signals


The block is able to generate three fault signals:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒInstrument is over-range

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒInstrument is under-range

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒInstrument is out-of-range (common signal)

Over-range and under-range faults are generated if the instrument is reading outside its normal 
calibrated range. Over-range if the instrument is reading higher than its maximum configured 
value and under-range if lower than its minimum configured value.

The levels at which the instrument is considered to be either over-range or under-range 
(out-of-range), are set as a configurable values passed to the module.

The out-of-range fault signal is a common signal that activates if either the over-range or 
under-range signal is active. It indicates the instrument is either over-range or under-range, but 
doesnâ€™t specify which.

1.2â€„ â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒSupervisory system interface


FC18001 is a Subroutine block used to scale an analog input. It does not have a supervisory
system interface.

blocks within the PAL. It is designed to provide a linear conversion of a raw analog input signal 
(in integer format) to a scaled value that represents the calibrated range of the instrument as a 
real (floating point) value in engineering units.

AI_RAW_SIGNAL is the input signal provided directly from the instrument itself (via input cards). 

The AI_RAW_DATA and AI_SCALE_DATA parameters are UDTs that hold information about the 
nature of the AI_RAW_SIGNAL, in the case of AI_RAW_DATA its input type: voltage, current &amp;c., 
its range in integer values and various parametric information and a textual description of the 
signal. In the case of AI_SCALE_DATA it specifies the scaled range of the signal, its engineering 
units, out-of-range values, a textual description of the instrument and the instrument tag itself.

â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•

Section 2.1.1 contains a full description of the AI_RAW_DATA and AI_SCALE_DATA parameters.

AI_SCALE_SIGNAL is the true scaled value of the analog input (AI_RAW_SIGNAL) in engineering 
units.

OVER_RANGE and UNDER_RANGE indicate if the signal is outside the permitted range. The limits at 
which under-range and over-range faults activate are provided as part of the information supplied 
via the AI_SCALE_DATA parameter

OVER_RANGE indicates the input is higher than the permitted tolerance and UNDER_RANGE 
indicates the input is lower than the permitted tolerance.

OUT_OF_RANGE is simply a common signal indicating the either OVER_RANGE or UNDER_RANGE 
is active.

This arrangement conforms with the PAL philosophy where IO card connections, safety signals 
and interlocks have unique formal parameters; all remaining signals are passed as variables 
within UDTs, see the Software Design Specification [Ref 008].

The scaled value is passed from the block as parameter: AI_SCALE_SIGNAL.

The scaled value (AI_SCALE_SIGNAL) is calculated as follows:


â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”
â”‚                              â€ƒâ€ƒ(AI_RAW_SIGNAL â”€ RAW_MIN) â•³ (SCALE_MAX â”€ SCALE_MIN)â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â”‚
â”‚AI_SCALE_SIGNAL =  â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•  â”¼ SCALE_MINâ€ƒâ€ƒâ”‚
â”‚â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ              â€ƒ       (RAW_MAX â”€ RAW_MIN)â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€„  â”‚
â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€  (2.1) â€†â”€â”€â”€â”˜

In the above calculation, RAW_MIN and RAW_MAX are preceded by AI_RAW_DATA. and SCALE_MIN and 
SCALE_MAX are preceded by AI_SCALE_DATA.

The three signals: AI_SCALE_SIGNAL, SCALE_MIN and SCALE_MAX are all floating-point numbers 
(real data type), the signals AI_RAW_SIGNAL, RAW_MIN and RAW_MAX are all integers (int data type).

Note:  â€ƒâ€ƒIt is assumed that the instrument has a linear response.

it holds the scaled range, instrument tag, signal description and as-sociated engineering unit 
information. Data is supplied to this parameter using DB00851_St_ConstAiScaleData, this 
contains a set of data each instrument configured for the project, each instrument being a 
dataset. E.g.

2.1.2  â€ƒâ€ƒ Configuration errors


The block requires that both the RAW_MAX/MIN and SCALE_MAX/MIN signals conform to certain 
rules:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ1.â€ƒâ€†RAW_MIN must be less than, and not equal to RAW_MAX
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ2.â€ƒâ€†SCALE_MIN must be less than, and not equal to SCALE_MAX

Should either of these conditions not be met, the three out of range parameters will all 
be activated (set true) 

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒOVER_RANGE
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒUNDER_RANGE
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒOUT_OF_RANGE

In addition, the AI_SCALE_SIGNAL signal will be set to zero irrespective of the AI_RAW_SIGNAL 
value.



â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚
2.2â€„ â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒOut of range signals


If the AI_SCALE_SIGNAL signal is outside the SCALE_MIN to SCALE_MAX range (red dotted area of 
the graph, Figure 2.1), the AI_SCALE_SIGNAL will still be calculated correctly; however, an 
appropriate, OVER_RANGE or UNDER_RANGE signal will be generated to indicate that the 
AI_SCALE_SIGNAL signal is outside the calibrated range of the instrument and is potentially no 
longer accurate.

Some tolerance is permitted before the OVER_RANGE and UNDER_RANGE signals are activated 
(most instruments are tolerant of slight over and under shoot readings).

The limits at which an over-range or under-range signal is generated is specified in the dataset 
passed to the module in the AI_SCALE_DATA parameter. Each such dataset is stored in 
DB00851_St_ConstAiScaleData (see Â§ 2.1.1) in the variables LIMIT_OVER and LIMIT_UNDER 
respectively. These represent the highest and lowest values that the scaled instrument value 
can read without being either over-range or under-range:

â€ƒAI_SCALE_DATA
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€†
â€ƒSIGNAL NAMEâ€†   â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒFUNCTION  â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒTYPE
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒLIMIT_UNDERâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ Lower limit of the scaled instrument value inâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€„Real
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒengineering units before instrument is 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒunder-range

â€ƒLIMIT_OVERâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€†Upper limit of the scaled instrument value inâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€„Real
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒengineering units before instrument is 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒover-range
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•



â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–
2.2.1  â€ƒâ€ƒ Common out of range signal


There is a third out of range signal: OUT_OF_RANGE, this signal is a common signal that just 
indicates the instrument is out of its calibrated range (it does not specify whether it is over or 
under range). 

It is activated if either the OVER_RANGE or UNDER_RANGE signal is active.

Note:  â€ƒâ€ƒIf a configuration error exists, see Â§ 2.1.2, all three out of range signals (OVER_RANGE, 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒUNDER_RANGE and OUT_OF_RANGE) will be activated irrespective of the 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒRAW_ANALOG value



â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–
2.2.2 â€ƒâ€ƒ Over and under range restrictions


The out-of-range limits passed to the module (AI_SCALE_DATA) must meet the following 
conditions:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒLIMIT_UNDER â‰¤ SCALE_MIN
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒLIMIT_OVER â‰¥ SCALE_MAX

I.e. the instrument cannot be considered either under range or over range if it is within the 
normal range of the instrument.

If the over-range limit (LIMIT_OVER) is less than SCALE_MAX, then itâ€™s value will be replaced by 
SCALE_MAX in all calculations. Similarly, if the under-range limit (LIMIT_UNDER) is greater than 
SCALE_MIN, then itâ€™s value will be replaced by SCALE_MIN in all calculations.



â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ”â”â”   â¬™â¬™â¬™â¬™â¬™â¬™   â”â”â”

It does not have a supervisory system interface.

MODIFICATION HISTORY


The revision data shown here, in the network comments, contains additional information 
reflecting the software development workflow under the version control system (VCS) employed 
to track all software changes.

The VCS in use is the Git Source Code Management system in conjunction with the GitHub online 
hosting system. The software in its entirety is available in the GitHub remote repository:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒhttps://github.com/practicalseries/PS2001-pal-software

Determines if a configuration error has occurred, this is true if either the RAW range or SCALED 
range has not been specified correctly, either:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒRAW_MAX &lt;= RAW_MIN (raw range error) OR
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒSCALE_MAX &lt;= SCALE_MIN (scaled range error)

If either, or both, conditions are true, the wrkConfigError signal is activated

                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
The out-of-range limits passed to the module (AI_SCALE_DATA) must meet the following 
conditions:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒLIMIT_UNDER â‰¤ SCALE_MIN
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒLIMIT_OVER â‰¥ SCALE_MAX

I.e. the instrument cannot be considered either under range or over range if it is within the 
normal range of the instrument.

If the over-range limit (LIMIT_OVER) is less than SCALE_MAX, then itâ€™s value will be replaced by 
SCALE_MAX in all calculations. Similarly, if the under-range limit (LIMIT_UNDER) is greater than 
SCALE_MIN, then itâ€™s value will be replaced by SCALE_MIN in all calculations.

The limits in use are stored in wrkLimitUnder and wrkLimitOver
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>

â”‚â€ƒAI_SCALE_SIGNAL =  â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•  â”¼ SCALE_MIN    â”‚

                  <Text>â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€â–€
The instrument is over range if the scaled value (stored in wrkReal) is greater than wrkLimitOver

The instrument is under range if the scaled value (stored in wrkReal)  is less than wrkLimitUnder

If either of these conditions is true, the common out of range signal is activated

Note:  â€ƒâ€ƒIf the range information is incorrect (wrkConfigError = TRUE),
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒThen all the out of range signals are activated (UNDER_RANGE, 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒOVER_RANGE and OUT_OF_RANGE) simultaneously
â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„â–„</Text>

TITLE:  â€ƒâ€ƒINSTRUMENTATION â€” ANALOG INSTRUMENT READ, SCALE AND MONITOR

â”‚â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ”‚

â”‚â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€„https://psop.uk/pal-smds-fc02001-p  â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â”‚

â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€ Ê·á´µá´°â»áµˆÊ°áµâ€†â”˜

FC02001_StdInstAnalogRead reads and scales an analog instrument signal received via 
an analog input card.

The resultant scaled value is a real (floating point) number that matches the calibrated range of 
the instrument in engineering units.

The block has the facility to generate up to four alarms and warnings whenever the signal is 
beyond a specific setpoint value (either above or below); the four signals are:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒAlarm high

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒWarning high

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒWarning low

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒAlarm low

Each alarm or warning can be time filtered (the condition must be present for a preset time 
before the alarm or warning is activated) and each will automatically reset when the signal is 
back within the acceptable range by a hysteresis amount.

In addition to the above four signals, various out-of-range fault signals will be generated if the 
instrument is outside its normal calibrated range by more than a specified percentage (this 
being a percentage of the total span of the instruments range).

The block can also generate an optional â€œexternal faultâ€ signal from a hardwired fault input from 
the instrument itself.

The block has a simulation mode whereby the scaled value is replaced by an operator selected 
value (over-writing any signal from the instrument). This can be used for testing purposes or if 
the instrument is out of service for any reason.

2.â€†â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒFUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION


This block is a comprehensive block designed to read and scale an analog instrument; it 
provides the following broad functions:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒRead an analog input, convert it to a real number that represents the calibrated 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒrange of the instrument in engineering units

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒGenerate high and low alarm and warning signals to indicate that the instrument is 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒabove or below specific thresholds

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒGenerate fault signals if the instrument is out of range or is indicating a specific fault 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒcondition

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒProvide simulation capabilities for testing and fault handling situations

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒGenerates the status and message signals necessary for symbolic representation at 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒa supervisory system (SCADA or HMI)



â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚â–‚
2.1â€„ â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒRead and scale and instrument signal


The principal function of the block is to read a raw integer signal from an analog instrument 
(in the form of an input word, IW), and convert it into a scaled, floating point (real) number that 
reflects the calibrated reading of the instrument in question.

For example, if a flow meter with a calibrated range of -100 l/s to +100 l/s provided a 4-20 mA 
signal to the PLC, then 4 mA would represent -100 l/s and 20 mA would represent +100 l/s.

A typical 4-20 mA analog input signal returns a raw value of 0 at 4 mA and 27648 at 20 mA.â€ƒ

The block would return scaled values as follows (it would also return every value in between; five 
typical values have been shown):

2.2â€„ â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒAlarms and warnings


The block provides four alarm/warning signals:


â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒALARM/WARNINGâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€†â€„FUNCTION
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒAlarm highâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€„Scaled signal is equal to or above a preset alarm high 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒthreshold (setpoint)

â€ƒWarning highâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€„Scaled signal is equal to or above a preset warning high
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒthreshold (setpoint)

â€ƒWarning lowâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  Scaled signal is equal to or above a preset warning low
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒthreshold (setpoint)

â€ƒAlarm lowâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ      Scaled signal is equal to or above a preset alarm low
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒthreshold (setpoint)
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•


Alarms and warnings are individually enabled and are individually configurable.

Each alarm or warning has a threshold value (the value at which it becomes active); high alarms 
and warnings are active when the instrument is at or above the threshold level, low alarms and 
warnings are active when the instrument is at or below the threshold level. 

Each alarm or warning also has a hysteresis value (the instrument must be inside the threshold 
value by at least the hysteresis amount before the alarm/warning is reset).

Alarms and warnings automatically reset once the instrument is inside the threshold value by at 
least the hysteresis value.

Each alarm or warning is equipped with on and off time filtering (to prevent nuisance triggering 
of alarms and warnings) where:

ON FILTERING:â€ƒâ€ƒDelays the activation of the alarm/warning (signal must
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€„be on for a time period before the block conditioned 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€„signal is activated).

OFF FILTERING: â€ƒ â€†Delays the alarm/warning from going off (i.e. the 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€„conditioned signal will remain on for a time period
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€„once the input is reset).

Each alarm and warning has its own configurable on and off filtering delays.

2.3â€„ â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒFault signals


The block is able to generate four fault signals:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒExternal fault
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒInstrument is over-range
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒInstrument is under-range
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒInstrument is out-of-range (common signal)

The external fault is generated by a hardwired signal from the instrument that indicates the 
instrument itself is reporting a fault. External fault signals are common with certain types of 
instruments (mass flow meters &amp;c.) and are used to indicate such things as medium not present 
(liquid flow meters) or calibration and maintenance issues (instrument requires calibrating or 
cleaning or some other form of servicing).

Over-range and under-range faults are generated if the instrument is reading outside its normal 
calibrated range. Over-range if the instrument is reading higher than its maximum permitted 
value and under-range if lower than its minimum permitted value.

The levels at which the instrument is considered to be either over-range or under-range 
(out-of-range), are set as a configurable values passed to the module.

The out-of-range fault signal is a common signal that activates if either the over-range or 
under-range signal is active. It indicates the instrument is either over-range or under-range, 
but doesnâ€™t specify which.

2.4â€„ â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒOperating modes


The block supports the following optional modes of operation:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒSimulation mode (allows the operator to override the current instrument reading 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒwith a simulated value)

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒRemote/local/all selection (allows control of the instrument to be restricted to a 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒspecific SCADA/HMI device) 

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒFaceplate disabled (disables all optional modes)

2.4.1  â€ƒâ€ƒ Simulation mode


The instrument can be switched to a simulation mode, in which the actual reading from the 
instrument is replaced by a simulated value provided by the operator. Simulation mode can be 
used during testing and can also be applied in a process environment if a fault condition is 
detected within the instrument.

Simulation mode is a manual operation that can only be initiated by an operator.



â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–â–
2.4.2  â€ƒâ€ƒ Remote/local/all mode


Remote and local operating modes refer to the device that has control of the instrument; where 
a plant has more than one SCADA/HMI, say a SCADA in a remote control room and a field 
mounted HMI local to the instrument, it is possible to restrict the control of the instrument to 
one, or the other, or both devices as follows:

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒRemoteâ€ƒOnly the remote system in the control room can control the device

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒLocalâ€ƒ   â€„A local system has taken control of the device and the remote system can 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  no longer issue commands to it

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€¢â€„ â€ƒâ€†Allâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ Any system can control the device

The default arrangement is for all system to have access to the device.

2.4.3  â€ƒâ€ƒ Faceplate disabled mode


Prevents the supervisory system from displaying the faceplate from which the above options are 
selected. If the faceplate is disabled, this module will set remote/local mode to ALL and will 
disable simulation mode.

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒpermanently to _False

â€ƒSTATIC_DATAâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€†Data structure that holds the configuration dataâ€ƒ  â€„UT02001    In
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒfor the instrument (raw range, scaled range 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒalarm and warning values, filtering times, 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒhysteresis values &amp;c.)

â€ƒDYNAMIC_DATAâ€ƒ    â€†Data structure that holds the live data for the â€ƒâ€ƒ  â€„UT22001    InOut
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒinstrument (its reading in engineering units, 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒany alarms or warnings that may be active, 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒcurrent timer values, selected operating 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒmode &amp;c.)
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•


AI_RAW_SIGNAL and EXT_FAULT are signals provided directly from the instrument itself (via 
input cards). The AI_RAW_DATA and AI_SCALE_DATA parameters are UDTs that hold information 
about the nature of the AI_RAW_SIGNAL, in the case of AI_RAW_DATA it specifies the input type: 
voltage, current &amp;c., its range in integer values and various parametric information and a 
textual description of the signal. In the case of AI_SCALE_DATA it specifies the scaled range of 
the signal, its engineering units, out-of-range values, a textual description of the instrument 
and the instrument tag itself.

Section 6 contains a full list of all variables within these UDTs.

This arrangement conforms with the PAL philosophy whereby IO card connections have unique 
formal parameters; all remaining signals are passed as variables within UDTs.

The AI_SCALE_DATA parameter


The AI_SCALE_DATA parameter is similar to the AI_RAW_DATA parameter except that in this case
it holds the scaled range, instrument tag, signal description and as-sociated engineering unit 
information. Data is supplied to this parameter using DB00851_St_ConstAiScaleData, this 
contains a set of data each instrument configured for the project, each instrument being a 
dataset. E.g.

User defined analog signal types


DB00801_St_ConstAiRawData contains a full set of analog card input ranges available to all 
Siemens Simatic analog input cards. However, if some non-Simatic card is being used 
(i.e. a third-party card that may have a Profinet or ProfiBus inter-face) it may be necessary to 
configure a user defined signal type.

User defined signal types are specified in the STATIC_DATA parameter, UDT variable 
USER_AI_RAW_DATA. This data will be used in place of any AI_RAW_DATA parameter in all 
calculations within the block, if and only if, the AI_RAW_DATA pa-rameter is set to dataset 
AI_RAW_0000 (identified by the AI_RAW_DATA.AI_CODE value being set to zero).

Under normal circumstances, the DYNAMIC_DATA variable actual_AiRawData is set to match 
the AI configuration supplied in the parameter AI_RAW_DATA. If, however, AI_RAW_DATA is set to 
dataset AI_RAW_0000 (identified by the AI_RAW_DATA.AI_CODE value being set to zero), then the 
data supplied in thee STATIC_DATA UDT variable STATIC_DATA.USER_AI_RAW_DATA is copied into 
the DYNAMIC_DATA variable actual_AiRawData.

In either case, the DYNAMIC_DATA variable actual_AiRawData always contains the configuration 
that is in use.

The STATIC_DATA parameter, UDT variable USER_AI_RAW_DATA is of UDT type 
UT00801_St_ConstAiRawData and contains all the same variables as the AI_RAW_DATA 
parameter. In the case of user defined signal types, the following variables within 
STATIC_DATA.USER_AI_RAW_DATA are not used and should be set to zero:

â€ƒSTATIC_DATA.USER_AI_RAW_DATA
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€†
â€ƒSIGNAL NAMEâ€†   â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒFUNCTION  â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒVALUE
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•

3.1.2  â€ƒâ€ƒ Configuration errors


The block requires that both the raw and scale range signals conform to certain rules::

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ1.â€ƒâ€†actual_AiRawData.RAW_MIN must be less than, and not equal to 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒactual_AiRawData.RAW_MAX 

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ2.â€ƒâ€†actual_AiScaleData.SCALE_MIN must be less than, and not equal to â€†
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒactual_AiScaleData.SCALE_MIN

Should either of these conditions not be met, the signal: status_ConfigError will be activated 
(set true), additionally the three out of range signals (see Â§ 3.4.1):

â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒmsg_Flt_OverRange
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒmsg_Flt_UnderRange
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒmsg_Flt_OutOfRange

will all be activated (this condition cannot be over-ridden by simulation mode, see Â§ 3.4.1) and 
the actual_Value will be set to zero irrespective of any values given to AI_RAW_SIGNAL.

Note:  â€ƒâ€ƒThis avoids the potential for a divide by zero error: if the RAW_MIN and 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒRAW_MAX are exactly equal, the calculation of the actual_Value in 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒequation (3.1) would result in a divide by zero error. </Text>

3.2â€„ â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒWarnings and alarms


By default, the block generates 4 alarms and warnings (2 warnings and 2 alarms, 4 in total) 
as follows:


â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒALARM / WARNINGâ€ƒâ€ƒ   FUNCTION
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒAlarm highâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€„Scaled signal is equal to or above a preset alarm high setpoint
â€ƒWarning highâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€„Scaled signal is equal to or above a preset warning high setpoint
â€ƒWarning lowâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒScaled signal is equal to or below a preset warning low setpoint
â€ƒAlarm lowâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒScaled signal is equal to or below a preset alarm low setpoint
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒDefault alarm and warning signals


The active state of any alarm or warning is stored in the DYNAMIC_DATA structure in the following 
variables:


â€ƒUT22001_Dy_InstAnalogRead
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒSIGNAL NAMEâ€†   â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒFUNCTION  â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒTYPE
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒmsg_Alm_Hâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€„MESSAGE â€” Alarm - high alarm is activeâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€„Bool
â€ƒmsg_Alm_Lâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   MESSAGE â€” Alarm - low alarm is activeâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ     Bool
â€ƒmsg_Wrn_Hâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€†MESSAGE â€” Warning - high warning is activeâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€„Bool
â€ƒmsg_Wrn_Lâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  â€„MESSAGE â€” Warning - low warning is activeâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ     Bool
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•


The alarms and warnings that end with _H are activated when the scaled instrument reading is 
greater than or equal to a setpoint threshold (i.e. activate when the measured quantity is too 
high; generally, if there is both an alarm high and a warning high, the convention within the PAL 
is that the warning should activate before the alarmÂ².


The alarms and warnings that end with _L are activated when the scaled instrument reading is 
less than or equal to a setpoint threshold (i.e. activate when the measured quantity is too low; 
generally, if there is both an alarm low and a warning low, the convention within the PAL is that 
the warning should activate before the alarmÂ².

â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
Â²  â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   â€„This is just a convention, there is nothing to stop the warning being set to occur after 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒthe alarm (i.e. the warning detecting the most extreme condition). All alarms and 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒwarnings are entirely independent of each other and no error checking is carried 
â€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒout to ensure that any particular threshold is above or below another.
â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•

All alarms and warnings are individually enabled (a disabled alarm or warning will never be 
activated), all alarms and warnings have individual setpoint values (the value at which the 
alarm or warning is triggered), all alarms and warnings have individual hysteresis valves 
(effectively a tolerance band, the difference between where an alarm activates and where it 
deactivates, used to prevent nuisance or â€œchatteringâ€ alarms). Finally, each alarm and warning 
has a configurable on and off delay (the alarm or warning will only activate if the reading is 
outside the threshold for the on-delay time and similarly will only deactivate when the reading 
is inside the threshold and hysteresis for the off-delay time).

The following table summarises all the available signals for each alarm and warning:


â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒSIGNALâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ  FUNCTIONâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ   TYPE   DETAILS
â€ƒâ€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•â€•
â€ƒCONFIG_XXX_Y_ENâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ Alarm/warning enabledâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€„Bool   â€†1 = enabled, 0 = disabled
â€ƒSP_XXX_Y_VALâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€†Alarm/warning setpoint valueâ€ƒ  â€„Realâ€ƒEngineering units
â€ƒSP_XXX_Y_HYST_VALâ€ƒâ€ƒ â€†Alarm/warning hysteresis valueâ€ƒRealâ€ƒEngineering units
â€ƒTIME_XXX_Y_ON_DELâ€ƒâ€ƒ Alarm/warning on delay timeâ€ƒâ€ƒâ€†Realâ€ƒIn seconds
â€ƒTIME_XXX_Y_OFF_DELâ€ƒ   â€†Alarm/warning off delay timeâ€ƒâ€ƒ Realâ€ƒIn seconds

The graph represents the scaled analog instrument reading, actual_Value (in engineering

If the alarm is enabled (CONFIG_ALM_H_EN = 1) then the following actions occur:
